summary: Feed s123_double to NDR is degraded: 100% VXLAN encapsulation (3177/3177 frames) hides inner traffic and 97.3% encrypted bytes exceeds 90% tolerance, leaving NDR with only outer headers/metadata and severely limiting detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding VXLAN-encapsulated traffic without stripping - 100% of frames arrive inside VXLAN. Source is likely a VTEP SPAN or broker tunnel-forwarding policy passing encapsulation straight to tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR sees only outer VXLAN/IP/UDP headers; inner Ethernet/IP/TCP and L7 payload are opaque so flow correlation, behavioral analytics and signature matching fail on all encapsulated traffic.

recommended_fix.why: Stripping VXLAN headers at the packet broker exposes inner L2-L7 frames to the NDR, restoring full parsing and detection without changing the TAP/SPAN source.

findings.root_cause: 97.26% of bytes are encrypted (threshold 90% for this NDR). Traffic is predominantly TLS and no decryption/key-sharing is performed before the NDR feed.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs full payload for deep inspection; with payload opaque it is limited to metadata/flow analysis and misses payload-based threats, C2, and exploit detection.

recommended_fix.why: Selective, policy-compliant TLS decryption or key/log forwarding before the NDR (decrypt zone on broker) is needed to provide cleartext where legally permitted and restore payload visibility.
